title: Springdale students featured in 'STEAM Sessions' at Bentonville Film Fest - NewsBreak
text: BENTONVILLE, Ark. (KNWA/KFTA) — “STEAM Sessions” at the Bentonville Film Festival on June 18 was particularly special for some local students who are just beginning their careers in the film industry. The sessions merge conversations on science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics, while also integrating filmmaking and storytelling. Multiple panels and workshops were offered as part of the event. One of those sessions highlighted students from Springdale Public Schools, who received cutting-edge education on media arts. “It’s all about the student finding the skill set that they then can use to have gainful employment after high school,” Trent Jones, the communications director for SPS said. “You can do film, you can do broadcast, you can do entrepreneurship, photography, graphic design.” The student’s specialized education is what landed them on the stage Wednesday afternoon, sharing their experiences. “The reason that it’s important to have them here is because they’re a product of the system, of the concept that we’re bringing to the table. What they did was they got their hands on early, they align their skills with their passion, and now they are graduating from school with the future in control of their hands,” Jones said. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to KNWA FOX24.
